newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast spot prods steady to higher Thurs.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast spot prods steady to higher Thurs.

text.p: Wholesale spot prices for U.S. West Coast products were steady to higher Thursday, as refineries increased buying on perceptions the market could not fall lower, traders said.
Prices for Los Angeles gasoline rose relative to San Francisco with several parcels of July CARB selling about a penny higher.
"It's starting to narrow a little bit," said one trader, referring to the difference between L.A. and the Bay area.
Distillates were generally flat, in sympathy with New York futures energy futures markets, which saw August crude oil fall 24 cents a barrel to $19.22.

At least two cargoes of July CARB gasoline sold to refineries in Los Angeles, at 53.75 cents and 55 cents a gallon, respectively, traders said. Traders talked the grade between 54.50 and 55.50 cents, one cent higher than Wednesday.
August barrels sold for about a penny higher than July, traders said, because of perceived excess supply this month.
Paper markets continued to trade briskly in August for hedging purposes, traders said.
A parcel of jet fuel sold in L.A. for about 54.50 cents a gallon.

A parcel of CARB gasoline sold for 55.50 cents a gallon, traders said, lowering the grade's price range one cent from yesterday. Bay area remained at a slight premium of 0.50 cents a gallon to Los Angeles, which is normally one to two cents higher.
Conventional grades in both cities were unchanged from Wednesday, traders said.
Reformulated gasoline, for sale in the metropolitan Phoenix area, was talked one cent below CARB levels,traders said.
